title: Agent tries to read a ticket for Frank

actors.label: AI agent
actors.description: An MCP client, e.g. a coding assistant

story.title: You asked the agent
story.what: Frank asked the agent to work with ticket 42.
story.why: The agent has no rights of its own here. It acts strictly on Frank's behalf.
story.matters: Every agent action traces back to a real person and inherits that person's limits.

story.title: The gateway brokered the request to the identity provider
story.what: The gateway presented Frank's identity and the agent's own credentials, asking for an Identity Assertion JWT (ID-JAG).
story.why: An agent can't mint its own access. Only the identity provider issues tokens, and only after evaluating policy.
story.matters: The exchange is the checkpoint: every agent action passes through policy before it can touch a resource.

story.title: The identity provider refused: no token
story.what: No access-policy rule for the ticket API matched Frank, so nothing was minted.
story.why: Frank isn't entitled to tickets, and the agent only ever borrows Frank's rights.
story.matters: The agent can't do what the user can't. The denial happens at the identity provider, before the API is ever reached.

story.title: The ticket API was never called
story.what: With no token, the call stopped at the identity provider.
story.why: There was nothing to present to the API.
story.matters: The resource is not the first line of defense. Policy is.

subtitle: Cross App Access: ID-JAG token exchange through an MCP gateway

outcome.headline: ✕ BLOCKED: NO TOKEN
outcome.detail: Frank matched no rule at the exchange, so no token was issued. The agent can't do what the user can't.
outcome.caption: no rule matched at the exchange · no token · API never reached
